title: The times they are a changing
author: PoopsMcScoots
selftext:
2021 : “Your game ideas have no value and no one wants to hear them.”

2026 : “Everyone stop posting your game ideas immediately!”

comments.author: SpicyBoyEnthusiast
comments.body: Most ideas are worthless. It's all about execution.

replies.author: No-Marionberry-772
replies.body: yeah this reaply hasnt changed as much as people think it has

replies.author: StoneCypher
replies.body: i've cranked out three 20 year old ideas this month because they were too much work and aren't anymore.

replies.author: No-Marionberry-772
replies.body:
Im not saying AI hasnt made it easier to implement ideas.

Im saying that ideas are complex, and implrmenting them, to a high degree of quality and depth, still need iteration, exploration, and revision.

The elevator pitch of your idea isnt the output, its the starting point and you build on it.

Everything is a lot faster now, but you still have to work through your ideas to fully develop them.

replies.author: StoneCypher
replies.body: i think you and i have very different opinions about gaming

replies.author: Col2k
replies.body:
your pong clone with waifus needs more depth, calculations, and polished features.

Im just playing, both sides of this argument have merit.

replies.author: StoneCypher
replies.body:
friend, if you knew how complicated game 3 was

but also, y'know, most successful games are actually simple games, in my experience.  it's the vampire survivors, not the world of warcrafts, that outnumber by count

replies.author: stjimmy96
replies.body:
I think it’s both. 

Take a game like Minecraft, its execution early days was definitely questionable, the game looked like crap and had so little content for so many years but the idea was brilliant and people loved it. 

Some other games have less unique/exciting ideas but they have a super execution which makes them stand out.

comments.author: TheReservedList
comments.body: They're still worthless lol.

replies.author: RiftInteractive
replies.body: How hard you want to cope ?

replies.author: TheReservedList
replies.body:
Lol, I sure am the one coping yes. All those incredibly original AI titles going around.

"My idea is offline world of warcraft with more loot! In fact, all my ideas are defined in terms of already existing games and they're amazing. A lot of RPGs where you can do anything you want!"

replies.author: Ordinary-Army-8523
replies.body: That's not a "game ideas are worthless" argument,  that's a "some ideas are worthless " argument.

replies.author: TheReservedList
replies.body: No. The most successful idea ever is having a plumber jump on turtles to save a princess. It’s 2% idea 98% execution.

replies.author: Ordinary-Army-8523
replies.body: That still doesn't equate to ideas being worthless. Without ideas, what exactly are you going to work on? You'll be refining nothingness I suppose.

replies.author: TheReservedList
replies.body: You can just copy someone else’s idea wholesale and iterate on it. That’s what Warcraft, the Last of Us and League of Legends have done.

replies.author: Ordinary-Army-8523
replies.body: Ok... you're still copying an idea, so it's clearly not worthless. If ideas are worthless, why copy them?

replies.author: TheReservedList
replies.body: You have it flipped. They are worthless in big part because they can be copied.

replies.author: Ordinary-Army-8523
replies.body: Execution can be copied as well, so by that logic execution is also worthless.

replies.author: TheReservedList
replies.body: How do you copy execution while making a different game? Sure you can copy execution by literally duplicating the files, but then that's just run of the mill piracy.

replies.author: Ordinary-Army-8523
replies.body: Let's say you like warcraft 3, you can make a game with the same mechanics and art style with just enough technical differences to be considered its own thing.

replies.author: TheReservedList
replies.body:
What technical difference? Because if you drop some of the units in Warcraft 3 and change their abilities slightly, game balance goes out the window. That's the execution part. You can't remove a undead unit and replace it with a healer. It's a cohesive whole. That is what makes great games and can never be "copied" without it being the same game.

Can you reskin Warcraft 3? Sure. But then you have the exact same game with different graphics.

replies.author: Ordinary-Army-8523
replies.body: You don't need to copy it exactly 1 to 1 in order to get similar results. But yes, you can quite literally just copy the gameplay and art style.

replies.author: TheReservedList
replies.body:
If you don't copy it 1:1 you will get shitty results because you won't understand what the reasons were for the decisions that lead to those mechanics being in the game were in the first place. Games aren't a pile of things. They're interconnected systems. You can't just discard one thing and add another and get something good.

That's what the people here who have never shipped a successful game fail to understand. It's also why most vibecoded games are: "I took CoD but added gun customization to it" or whatever.

replies.author: Ordinary-Army-8523
replies.body:
"
If you don't copy it 1:1 you will get shitty results because you won't understand what the reasons were for the decisions that lead to those mechanics being in the game were in the first place"

You're making a lot of assumptions about me and what I do or do not understand.

replies.author: TheReservedList
replies.body: You can't possibly understand why the decisions in a game you didn't make were made without going to the same process the people who made the game did. It has nothing to do with me or you.

replies.author: Ordinary-Army-8523
replies.body:
You are correct that unless a developer speaks out, I have no way of truly knowing what they thought when making their design decisions. For all I know, the game carefully crafted stats on a monster could just be a "good enough" last minute addition. 

However that doesn't really matter because if the end product resonates with me
, I am perfectly capable of studying it and reverse engineering the thought process behind why I personally find it enjoyable.  


Then I can repeat the thought process to create more similar content that is faithful enough in spirit which will appeal to me and others.

replies.author: TheReservedList
replies.body: Yes, that's theoretically possible. That's also significantly harder to do than just making your own game from design first principles so I'm not sure why you would go through that full reverse engineering.

replies.author: KrakatauaMAN123
replies.body:
Ideas are worthless until they are explored in depth. That's where they start generating value.

Most people don't have ideas worth exploring nor the skill to do so if they have one that is.

An idea as a single thing is worthless.

You can build on someone's explored idea and add value or just be the tree branch that is rotting

Not everything has to be a brand new invention. People can create with AI tools. Some people create really amazing things. Have you been to the Midjourney feed? There are some beautiful pieces in there.

replies.author: TheReservedList

See my previous statement.

replies.body: I’m unhinged? Your comments keep getting deleted because you’re crashing out at humans over AI. Might be time to go outside and take some deep clearing breaths.

replies.body: None of my comments have been deleted. Also I love AI and am not crashing out about it.

replies.author: mermaidreefer
replies.body: Hehehe sure Jan. I see the comments you make and then I navigate to them and the one where you called me a nasty name got deleted. You should really chill.

replies.author: eduo
replies.body:
Correction: "A lot of games that don't force you to do the thing I was bad at" :D 

With AI we're seeing all the people with mediocre ideas that in the past had been blocked by artists and developers realize their ideas were indeed mediocre when they finally bring them to release and nobody is interested. 

There's this very popular Meme in Spain about how "in his head, it sounded great" that comes to my mind every time someone wonders why their unoriginal and half-baked idea is not taking off.

replies.author: eduo
replies.body:
Don't be confused. What's changed is that you don't need to get anyone involved into bringing bad ideas into the world. But bad ideas are still bad ideas.

It doesn't mean all AI games are bad games but it does mean all bad ideas are still bad ideas.

The second most common post in several subs revolving around AI development is the realization that your pet project is of no interest to most people and that with AI you just made it faster for you to find out.

There's nothing to "cope" with. This is an AI-friendly sub. It doesn't mean pandering to mediocrity, though.

Bad Ideas and AI have nothing in common but AI makes it easy to prove if they were bad to begin with. Many were, and it becomes proven.

replies.author: shuozhe
replies.body:
AI UX still sucks, getting better, but still nowhere close to fluid. What AI is amazing at is to copy open source games, see all the flight simulator one shots.

But a game designer or UX guy can complete a game without coder

comments.author: BotherResponsible378
comments.body:
Everyone has an idea. And everyone thinks their idea is gold. 

And yet, even before AI most games that release are failures. That's not going to change just because AI came out.

replies.author: cxfoulke
replies.body: Yeah like the thing people are really stealing isn't... The idea it's more the millions of social media impressions and viral moment.

replies.author: Ancient_Dot_599
replies.body: Yea but more people means more failures but also more successes, a lot more

replies.author: BotherResponsible378
replies.body:
That's overly optimistic. Just because someone has an idea for a game doesn't mean they know how to make a game. AI I can do a lot of work but AI isn't going to make good design for you. 

Ai is a tool, it's not a wish granting genie.

replies.author: 2FastHaste
replies.body: But on a "tool to wish granting genie spectrum", every year it will move slightly more towards the genie end.

replies.author: BotherResponsible378
replies.body:
And once it moves towards the genie end, it won't matter whether or not you have an idea and it's good. 

Because then everybody's idea will be good, and we will be engulfed in things. No one will care about your game when everybody can make a game that good because they aren't actually making it. And AI is. 

At that point, making really good games is going to be like an artist who's really good who can't get work and has to do another job anyway. You might get some followers but that's about it. Making games at that point will just be a hobby.

You must have seen the Incredibles. Whenever one's super, no one will be.

replies.author: 2FastHaste
replies.body:
>No one will care about your game when everybody can make a game that good because they aren't actually making it. And AI is.

I will. The reason I care is the actual intrinsic game. I'm not pretending to like games while using them as a proxy for other things. (yes I understand I'm in a minority but my perspective is just as valid)

>Whenever one's super, no one will be.

Good. That's what I wish for society in general. Egalitarianism and the end of meritocracy.

replies.author: BotherResponsible378
replies.body:
I said you will care about the games you make. Because it'll just be a hobby at that point. 

And you and I have very different views of how we want society to go. I very strongly disagree with that attitude. In a perfect world where humans don't need to worry about any resources and we all live comfortably, I still get enjoyment out of watching. Humans perform better than other humans. To me. Games, movies shows, it's like watching sports.

replies.author: Unfair-Ad9415
replies.body: Successes are a matter of demand. People arent playing more games than before

replies.author: 2FastHaste
replies.body: Success can also be meant as in succeeding to make a good game rather than commercially succeeding.

replies.author: Unfair-Ad9415
replies.body: Fair enough

replies.author: Greed_444
replies.body: Well i want my idea to be a game so i can play it, not really because i want to share it

replies.author: BotherResponsible378
replies.body:
Everybody is going to have their own opinion on this. That might work for you. And that eventuality might be good for you. 

But for the people who think that this is going to allow them to become a big game designer and make a living doing this, they are woefully mistaken.

replies.author: Maple-Syrup89
replies.body: I disagree. Some game creators WILL be able to be break out indies, and the ones using AI will be more likely, since they can get to market faster with new ideas.

replies.author: BotherResponsible378
replies.body:
It doesn't seem like you understand what I'm actually saying. Because your comment doesn't have anything to do with the point that I'm actually making. You jumped mid conversation and seems like you only acknowledged part of the last comment that I made. And don't really understand the context of the conversation that was happening or the point that was being made in general.

The point that I'm making is that people who are treating AI like it's going to make their idea good or foolish. Good games succeeds and because the people who are making them understand how to make good games. 

If you don't know how to make a good game, AI is not going to help your idea succeed. The games that will succeed are games that are designed well by people who know what they're doing. Whether they're using AI, traditional methods, or a blend of both. 

AI is not going to magically make a bad idea a good one.

-

Also, your point about speed doesn't really make any sense. If a good game goes to market, it's going to succeed whether it took 2 years or 6 months to make. Games don't succeed because they come out faster or slower. They succeed based on the quality of the game. That's just true of all things.

The speed at which you produce a game has no weight on whether or not people are going to enjoy it when it is finally out.

replies.author: Maple-Syrup89
replies.body:
I read all 4 sentences above you, and I disagreed with the premise of this specific comment. And this is fucking reddit man, people can jump in at any level. Welcome to the site. 

  
I agree with you, AI doesn't make a good game, but it enables people with good ideas and good taste to make more games more quickly. And some of those people will make it big. 

  
I never claimed it will make bad ideas good. I said it will help get more to market more quickly but some will rise to the top, as they did before AI, its just faster now. Faster bullshit, and faster greatness. 

  
You misunderstand speed. A good game dev might have to make 5 games before one really finds success. They can do that in 2 years instead of 10 now. Thats getting to market faster with their ideas, to either flop or fly.

replies.author: BotherResponsible378
replies.body:
People can jump in at any level, but then they make comments that don't make sense as a response. That's what I was pointing out about yours. Your comment didn't make sense because it didn't have anything to do with what I was talking about. I'm not arbitrarily pointing out that you jumped in the middle, I'm arbitrarily pointing out that your comment didn't make sense and so therefore it doesn't feel like you understood what I was saying which leads me to believe that you didn't actually read what was happening.

You now go on to agree with the point that I was actually making.

But yes, I do agree with what you're saying now. How you've reworded what you said. Good games are going to succeed. It won't matter how they're being made.

I think that there is actually far too much AI versus not AI game development conversation. The real conversation is about indie gaming in general. In my opinion. Even before AI, technology is flat and the ability for people to produce games. It's why the indie market has been growing and been so robust over the last few years. I don't think it's going to matter whether the games are made with AI or not. I think that indie is the future of gaming.

replies.author: Maple-Syrup89
replies.body: Skilled 10 man studios will compete with 100 person teams of 5 years ago. The bottleneck will be large scoped games where even skilled creators will be limited by time to make good content. Thats my prediction anyways. I think we will see far more novel ideas and great storytelling coming to market in the meantime, not megacorps rehashing the same sanitized 5 games over and over.

replies.author: BotherResponsible378
replies.body:
I agree. I just think that that's going to happen whether people are making it with AI or not. Because it already is. The indie gaming market is just way more interesting than the AAA market.

Most AAA games just don't interest me anymore. But there's a long list of indie games that I haven't had time to play. As far as I'm concerned, major corporations can get bent.

replies.author: AnotherMisanthrope
replies.body: Agreed but let’s add some balance too. Let’s not pretend that only cream has risen to the top. There’s CoD slop, Madden slop, loot box and seasonal pass slop. People love slop and plenty of good and even great games get buried under mainstream pop-slop.

replies.author: BotherResponsible378
replies.body:
I don't disagree with that. I mean there's lots of games that I for instance would consider slopp that other people just don't. But that's also preference right? Like that's not quantifiable in any way other than preference. What I was saying is ultimately the market will determine whatever is going to ride to rise to the top, and for instance, regardless whether or not I like fortnite, I can acknowledge the very specific nature of its design that makes it successful as well as call of duty or any other game versus games that just actually aren't good. And I do think that there's a very big difference between kind of what might seem to you and me as a mediocre game, and what other people get enjoyment out of. 

What I'm referencing not succeeding are the people who literally don't know how to make a game and don't understand the gravity of what it takes to actually make a game. You know that's important. That's hard to get. It's hard to understand until you kind of fail a lot and then you start to realize how little you understand about making games.

For a very long time most of my life I thought I had brilliant ideas about things to make. Then I began making things and now I'm sitting on the other side of the veil where I understand what makes something good and what makes something bad significantly more than I did before. And I look at my previous naivete with revulsion. 

People who are just going to use AI to make games without learning how to actually make a game are never actually going to get good at it. Or more so the odds are significantly stacked against them. The people who are going to get the most out of AI when making games are the people who know how to make games and then use AI to make those games. 

I actually saw a post I think on here yesterday, where someone was saying remember when you're making your AI game do these things and they put a list of things that are just the things you should do if you're making a game no matter what. Whether it's with AI or not. And those are a lot of things that a lot of people who want to make games with AI or without. Don't realize that you need to do and consider.

replies.author: pinky_monroe
replies.body: This is incredibly real. I’ve had so many ideas run into dead ends. It’s frustrating

replies.author: BotherResponsible378
replies.body:
People who know what they're doing, always run into dead ends. That's part of being an experienced or seasoned developer is knowing that not every idea pans out. 

And knowing when to throw in the towel and start something new. And all of this is true for people who use AI to make games or who people who don't. The tools being used don't change that reality.

replies.author: HazelCheese
replies.body:
CoD is not slop.

It's monetisation is slop but the actual game itself is extremely well designed. From everything to do with how it sounds to how aiming and shooting feels. It's miles better than 99% of games and they pour millions of dollars of resources into achieving that.

I seriously suggest googling and reading David Camplands UI spec for Halo3 that he posted. There is a huge amount of work that goes into making a game "feel" good. Without that kind of work games like Halo or CoD wouldn't be known at all.

replies.author: AggroSolo
replies.body: The failure rate was never about ideas, it's scoping and finishing

replies.author: BotherResponsible378
replies.body:
It's very foolish to think that everyone who has a game idea has a good game idea. 

That's not true about literally. Any ideas about anything. Lots of people have really bad ideas all the time. You can't possibly actually have that opinion if you've been following any indie game subs at all in the past ever. There are an awful lot of boring uninteresting or bad ideas That have reached completion and faced the market and then failed. 

Do you know how many games released on steam every year? One estimation puts it as above 19,000. I'm going to bet that you don't know most of those games.

comments.author: cxfoulke
comments.body:
No one cares about your idea... Posted to a social media with 15 followers or a random reddit. 

If your idea goes viral and gets millions of impressions and wishlists that's a valuable commodity that people will try to steal. 

99% of game ideas are worthless. 

Like an idea that captures a moment valuable, it's final fantasy but all the enemies are hot anime babes worthless. 

It's been this way forever... If in the pass you go to a publisher etc  just I have this really cool idea is worthless.

comments.author: javierthhh
comments.body: I learned that more people than I thought had  ADHD. Everyone wants to make the same Minecraft dungeon copy

comments.author: completelypositive
comments.body: Ideas are still a dime a dozen.

comments.author: Negative-Tear5402
comments.body:
OP, I think you're seriously misunderstanding the situation. 

Sure, non programmers have an easier barrier to entry to getting a game out there. But you do realize there are a million people like you who are thinking the exact same thing? So now you have a market that is flooded with these games that have been executed by non programmers with AI, people who had no prior game development experience. To add on top of it, the way AI executes ideas is roughly the same despite who uses it (the more vibe coded, the more obvious). That means you have all these games that look and feel the same. 

And the truth of the matter is, players can recognize it, and they get tired of it real quick. That doesn't mean you have to stop, you're more than welcome to try your idea out. But I bet you're going to have a huge problem in getting people to play your game. 

Do you know what the most economically rewarding for AI and game dev is? Experienced software engineers who develop the games, who use AI to pump out tedious code more quickly. 

You're forgetting that the experienced people also have access to AI, and you can bet they do a much better job than inexperienced people.

You can work on your pet project, but I think you have to be realistic

replies.body: Yeah I think the fact we still don't have a single groundbreaking popular ai only game says everything. Where are the "idea guys" at suddenly?

replies.body: I agree, but i think its due to the fact that truly popular AI games will have to be worked on for a long time, just like real games. Even AI wont make making a great game instant!

comments.body: If you believe this then I have a billion dollar open world crafting survival idea for you

comments.author: Weeros_

AI hasn’t made good execution easier, on the contrary I would argue it has raised the bar quite a lot. In other words, the ratio of games where their idea is executed well to those where it’s executed poorly is gonna go down, not up.

replies.body:
>More like I don't want to continue the conversation with someone who thinks they can build something good with a shit idea and a good execution.

replies.author: SicklyNick
replies.body: Tip your fedora and move on

replies.author: bakalidlid
replies.body:
Execution is in the details brother. Execution is knowing that cutting the startup frames of your attack anim makes it snappier. Its knowing that something should be changed because it reads wrong. Its removing a single enemy out of a room because you played it repeatedly, and you were juuuuuuust about to start getting annoyed. Its removing a light in a room because there was nothing there and players kept walking there anyway, wasting time.  a game or anything else is like:

So here is what I think, Ideas alone have always been worthless, it's always been in the execution. And while now execution has become easier it still doesn't guarantee Quality. 10 People can bring the same idea to life but in the end maybe only 1 will do it great, the rest will be mediocre.

It's that way in all areas of Business, I can have a great Idea for a Donut shop, but if I don't execute it it's worthless.

Also I for one kinda like that crazy shit that is coming to life lately, some weird shit that no one in their right mind would have made, but somehow some of them work, they are fun as crazy as they are!

But what excites me the most about AI is all the old shit that is being brought back to life, the games that we used to play, and a lot of people still play. But without the bugs, without the missing features. Games that have been abandoned by their creators for one reason or another.

And what I like most of all is, that the little guy can take on the BIG GUYS now, anyone can make a AAA game in their Bedroom now over a weekend or a few months, whatever time it takes. But they can for sure do it without Millions and Millions in funding.

So I say bring it on, let's see all those crazy ass games come to life, bring back the old ones, bring back fun games!

This expression is and always has been an over-simplification. Good game ideas never were worthless, but the problem is that people who think they have a good idea but can't code usually don't realize their idea is shit.

A good game designer / director is incredibly valuable, but a bad one is worse than useless. And now that people can make things with AI they're realizing how true that is. 99% of the things people make are shit because even if the game does manage to get made, they never realized until now that their idea wasn't worth making to begin with.
